spec.description: deck.gl's taxi-trips example replayed over lit 3D buildings of Lower Manhattan.

options.content:
# Lower Manhattan in motion

996 yellow-cab trips replayed over the buildings of Lower Manhattan. Each trail is one taxi:
the bright head is where the cab is now, and the tail fades behind it. **Press play on the
map's clock**; drag with the right button to orbit.

The data is the example that ships with deck.gl ([visgl/deck.gl-data](https://github.com/visgl/deck.gl-data/tree/master/examples/trips)),
read in place from GitHub once per visit, into your own browser, where [Chaski](https://github.com/ubica-ecuador/chaski) runs every query on this page. Its timestamps count seconds from an unnamed start, so the
clock runs from 00:00 to 00:41 and says nothing about the real hour. The sample was cut at the
30-minute mark — 279 trips end within ten seconds of it — which is why the count below falls off a
cliff there. **Drag across that curve** to replay only that window of it: the map, its clock and the figures keep just the stretch of each trip inside it, cut at the window's edges; *Median trip* stays the whole trip's duration. **Click a vendor** under the curve to leave its cabs out of the map and the figures.

spec.rawSql:
WITH w AS (
  SELECT coalesce(try_cast($t_lo AS DOUBLE), '-infinity'::DOUBLE) AS lo,
         coalesce(try_cast($t_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE) AS hi,
         -- The vendors hidden in the curve's legend: '0', '1' or '0,1'.
         string_split($vendors_off, ',') AS off
),
sel AS (SELECT t.* FROM $trips t, w
         WHERE t.t_end > w.lo AND t.t_start < w.hi AND NOT list_contains(w.off, t.vendor::VARCHAR)),
pts AS (SELECT n, unnest(path) AS p, unnest(timestamps) AS ts, generate_subscripts(timestamps, 1) AS i FROM sel),
-- Every leg between two consecutive GPS points that is driven inside the
-- window, and the share of it at which it enters (f0) or leaves (f1) the window
-- when it crosses an edge. Without a window both stay NULL: the CASE keeps the
-- infinite edges out of the arithmetic.
legs AS (
  SELECT n, i, ta, tb, pa, pb, lo, hi,
         CASE WHEN ta < lo THEN (lo - ta) / (tb - ta) END AS f0,
         CASE WHEN tb > hi THEN (hi - ta) / (tb - ta) END AS f1
  FROM (SELECT n, i, ts AS ta, p AS pa, lead(ts) OVER tw AS tb, lead(p) OVER tw AS pb
        FROM pts WINDOW tw AS (PARTITION BY n ORDER BY i)), w
  WHERE tb > lo AND ta < hi
),
-- Each leg cut to the window: an end outside it moves along the leg to the
-- edge; an end inside it stays the GPS point it was.
cut AS (
  SELECT n, i, f0, f1,
         CASE WHEN f0 IS NULL THEN ta    ELSE lo END                          AS t0,
         CASE WHEN f0 IS NULL THEN pa[1] ELSE pa[1] + (pb[1] - pa[1]) * f0 END AS lng0,
         CASE WHEN f0 IS NULL THEN pa[2] ELSE pa[2] + (pb[2] - pa[2]) * f0 END AS lat0,
         CASE WHEN f1 IS NULL THEN tb    ELSE hi END                          AS t1,
         CASE WHEN f1 IS NULL THEN pb[1] ELSE pa[1] + (pb[1] - pa[1]) * f1 END AS lng1,
         CASE WHEN f1 IS NULL THEN pb[2] ELSE pa[2] + (pb[2] - pa[2]) * f1 END AS lat1
  FROM legs
),
-- The trail, point by point: a GPS point shared by two legs counts once.
ends AS (
  SELECT n, i + CASE WHEN f0 IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 0.25 END AS k, t0 AS ts, lng0 AS lng, lat0 AS lat, f0 IS NULL AS measured FROM cut
  UNION
  SELECT n, i + CASE WHEN f1 IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0.75 END,      t1,       lng1,        lat1,        f1 IS NULL             FROM cut
),
-- Trips on the road at some moment of the window, and each one's whole span.
road AS (SELECT * FROM sel WHERE n IN (SELECT n FROM cut)),
clock AS (SELECT s FROM (SELECT unnest(range(0, 2490, 10)) AS s), w WHERE s BETWEEN w.lo AND w.hi)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM road)                                 AS "Trips",
       -- Measurements only: the points drawn at the window's edges are not.
       (SELECT count(*) FROM ends WHERE measured)::BIGINT          AS "GPS points",
       -- The legs as cut to the window, haversine as in the dataset; tenths
       -- below 10 km, so a quiet minute does not read as standing still.
       (SELECT coalesce(CASE WHEN km < 10 THEN round(km, 1) ELSE round(km) END, 0)
        FROM (SELECT sum(2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(
                power(sin(radians(lat1 - lat0) / 2), 2) + cos(radians(lat0)) * cos(radians(lat1)) * power(sin(radians(lng1 - lng0) / 2), 2)))) AS km
              FROM cut))                                           AS "Km driven",
       -- A trip's whole duration, not the stretch inside the window.
       (SELECT round(median(t_end - t_start) / 60, 1) FROM road)  AS "Median trip, min",
       (SELECT coalesce(max(c), 0) FROM (SELECT count(*) AS c FROM clock JOIN road ON s BETWEEN t_start AND t_end GROUP BY s))
                                                                   AS "Most taxis at once"

-- Pinned to midnight UTC on 1 January 2026, the zone kepler's clock shows,
-- so it reads 00:00 to 00:41.
WITH w AS (
  SELECT coalesce(try_cast($t_lo AS DOUBLE), '-infinity'::DOUBLE) AS lo,
         coalesce(try_cast($t_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE) AS hi,
         -- The vendors hidden in the curve's legend: '0', '1' or '0,1'.
         string_split($vendors_off, ',') AS off
),
sel AS (SELECT t.* FROM $trips t, w
         WHERE t.t_end > w.lo AND t.t_start < w.hi AND NOT list_contains(w.off, t.vendor::VARCHAR)),
pts AS (SELECT n, unnest(path) AS p, unnest(timestamps) AS ts, generate_subscripts(timestamps, 1) AS i FROM sel),
-- Every leg between two consecutive GPS points that is driven inside the
-- window, and the share of it at which it enters (f0) or leaves (f1) the window
-- when it crosses an edge. Without a window both stay NULL: the CASE keeps the
-- infinite edges out of the arithmetic.
legs AS (
  SELECT n, i, ta, tb, pa, pb, lo, hi,
         CASE WHEN ta < lo THEN (lo - ta) / (tb - ta) END AS f0,
         CASE WHEN tb > hi THEN (hi - ta) / (tb - ta) END AS f1
  FROM (SELECT n, i, ts AS ta, p AS pa, lead(ts) OVER tw AS tb, lead(p) OVER tw AS pb
        FROM pts WINDOW tw AS (PARTITION BY n ORDER BY i)), w
  WHERE tb > lo AND ta < hi
),
-- Each leg cut to the window: an end outside it moves along the leg to the
-- edge; an end inside it stays the GPS point it was.
cut AS (
  SELECT n, i, f0, f1,
         CASE WHEN f0 IS NULL THEN ta    ELSE lo END                          AS t0,
         CASE WHEN f0 IS NULL THEN pa[1] ELSE pa[1] + (pb[1] - pa[1]) * f0 END AS lng0,
         CASE WHEN f0 IS NULL THEN pa[2] ELSE pa[2] + (pb[2] - pa[2]) * f0 END AS lat0,
         CASE WHEN f1 IS NULL THEN tb    ELSE hi END                          AS t1,
         CASE WHEN f1 IS NULL THEN pb[1] ELSE pa[1] + (pb[1] - pa[1]) * f1 END AS lng1,
         CASE WHEN f1 IS NULL THEN pb[2] ELSE pa[2] + (pb[2] - pa[2]) * f1 END AS lat1
  FROM legs
),
-- The trail, point by point: a GPS point shared by two legs counts once.
ends AS (
  SELECT n, i + CASE WHEN f0 IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 0.25 END AS k, t0 AS ts, lng0 AS lng, lat0 AS lat, f0 IS NULL AS measured FROM cut
  UNION
  SELECT n, i + CASE WHEN f1 IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0.75 END,      t1,       lng1,        lat1,        f1 IS NULL             FROM cut
)
-- Only the stretch of each trip inside the window, so kepler's timeline spans
-- the window too: whole trips would stretch it back to their first point.
SELECT 'trip ' || n                     AS trip_id,
       'Vendor ' || vendor              AS vendor,
       to_timestamp(1767225600 + ends.ts) AS time,
       lat                              AS latitude,
       lng                              AS longitude,
       round(km, 2)                     AS trip_km,
       round((t_end - t_start) / 60, 1) AS trip_min
FROM ends JOIN sel USING (n)
ORDER BY n, k

-- How many cabs are mid-trip at each moment, every ten seconds, by vendor.
-- Always the whole clock: the brush is drawn over it, not applied to it.
WITH clock AS (SELECT unnest(range(0, 2490, 10)) AS s)
SELECT s,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE t.vendor = 0) AS v0,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE t.vendor = 1) AS v1
FROM clock LEFT JOIN $trips t ON s BETWEEN t.t_start AND t.t_end
GROUP BY s
ORDER BY s

spec.description: Cabs mid-trip at each moment, counted every ten seconds; the bar marks the instant the map is playing. Hover it and the map marks where each cab was at that moment; hovering the map's clock opens the curve at its time. Drag across it to replay only that window: the map, its clock and the figures keep the stretch of each trip inside it, cut at the window's edges, while Median trip stays the whole trip's duration. The toolbar at the top right clears it. Click a vendor in the legend to leave its cabs out of the map and the figures.

source.sql:
-- deck.gl's own trips example, read once into the viewer's browser: one row
-- per trip. Timestamps are seconds from an unnamed start.
WITH raw AS (
  SELECT row_number() OVER () AS n, vendor::INTEGER AS vendor, path, timestamps
  FROM read_json('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/visgl/deck.gl-data/master/examples/trips/trips-v7.json', maximum_object_size = 100000000)
  WHERE len(path) >= 2 AND len(path) = len(timestamps)
),
pts AS (SELECT n, unnest(path) AS p, generate_subscripts(path, 1) AS i FROM raw),
prev AS (
  SELECT n, radians(p[2]) AS lat, radians(p[1]) AS lng,
         radians(lag(p[2]) OVER w) AS lat0, radians(lag(p[1]) OVER w) AS lng0
  FROM pts WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY n ORDER BY i)
),
-- Haversine by hand, on the radius ST_Distance_Sphere uses: calling that would
-- make the browser fetch the spatial extension, seconds for one column.
km AS (
  SELECT n, sum(coalesce(2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(
           power(sin((lat - lat0) / 2), 2) + cos(lat0) * cos(lat) * power(sin((lng - lng0) / 2), 2))), 0)) AS km
  FROM prev GROUP BY n
)
SELECT raw.n, vendor, path, timestamps,
       timestamps[1]::DOUBLE AS t_start, timestamps[-1]::DOUBLE AS t_end,
       len(path) AS points, km.km
FROM raw JOIN km USING (n)

-- The footprints and heights that ship beside the trips in deck.gl's example.
-- Each ring is a bare list of [lng, lat]; closed here so it reads as WKT.
WITH raw AS (
  SELECT height, CASE WHEN polygon[1] = polygon[-1] THEN polygon
                      ELSE list_append(polygon, polygon[1]) END AS ring
  FROM read_json('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/visgl/deck.gl-data/master/examples/trips/buildings.json', maximum_object_size = 100000000)
  WHERE len(polygon) >= 3
)
SELECT height AS height_m,
       'POLYGON((' || array_to_string(list_transform(ring, c -> c[1] || ' ' || c[2]), ', ') || '))' AS geom
FROM raw
